data.title: Sanofi Gets U.S. Approval for Rare Disease Drug
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Sanofi received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for a new drug for a rare inherited disorder called Gaucher disease, the first treatment for neurological symptoms caused by the condition.

The French drugmaker said late Wednesday that its medicine, marketed under the Infilbray brand and also known as venglustat, was authorized in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kilograms--or 33 pounds--for type 3 Gaucher disease, one of the three major forms of the disease.

The FDA said type 3 Gaucher disease affects the brain and nervous system as harmful substances build up in the brain, causing difficulties with coordination, speech and thinking that can worsen over time.

Sanofi said Infilbray is a once-daily oral medicine designed to act across the blood-brain barrier, targeting the abnormal accumulation of fatty substances called glycosphingolipids.

A late-stage clinical trial showed the drug led to significant improvements in certain neurological manifestations of the disease like cognitive deficits and difficulty with coordination and balance, the company said.

Sanofi said Infilbray carries warnings and precautions for suicidal ideation and behavior, clouding of vision in younger patients, and adverse effects on fetal development during pregnancy.

data.title: Blue Star, Voltas, LG Electronics shares rally up to 8% after key input material sells off globally
data.description:
Shares of consumer durable stocks Voltas, Blue Star, LG Electronics India, Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals, and Havells India rose up to 8% on Thursday, November 19, after the prices of Copper, a key input material, slipped to the lowest level in seven months, thereby reversing all the gains seen in 2026 so far.

Copper is a key raw material used by the consumer durable companies. Lower copper prices would reduce the cost of manufacturing ACs and other appliances. The decline in prices will support gross margins and lower the input cost pressure seen so far.

As a result, companies may avoid further price hikes to protect volumes.

In 2026, the companies have hiked their prices by 10% - 12% to offset the commodity price inflation.

Blue Star told CNBC-TV18 earlier that input price inflation is painful and that the first quarter was tough and the second quarter continued to be painful with regards to margins.

The margins of the consumer durable companies were hit due to higher raw material prices:

Stock reactions

Voltas shares were trading 8% higher on Thursday at ₹1,225 apiece on Thursday. The stock has risen 20.2% in the past month and has therefore trimmed its 2026 loss down to 11%.

Blue Star shares are trading with gains of 6% to ₹1,716.8. The stock is now down only 3% for the year so far, having gained nearly 9.5% in the last one month.

Shares of LG Electronics were trading 1.5% higher at 1,705 apiece. The stock is up 14.8% this year, so far.

Shares of Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals were trading 4.7% higher at 217.02 apiece. The stock has risen 4.2% in the past month but is fallen 12.9% this year, so far.

Havells India shares were trading 4.1% higher at 1,186.9 apiece. The stock has risen 7.6% in the past month but is still down 16.2% this year, so far.

data.title: NLC India's green energy unit files for IPO
data.description:
State-run miner NLC India's unit NLC India Renewables (NLCD.NS) has filed for an initial public offering, according to draft papers.

  • NLC India, the state-run lignite miner and power producer that operates under the Ministry of Coal, is offloading 100 million shares in its green energy unit, according to the prospectus dated Wednesday

  • NLC India Renewables plans to sell new shares worth 33 billion rupees ($353.14 million) in the offering and the proceeds are earmarked for debt repayment

  • The green-energy arm develops solar and wind projects as part of its parent's push to expand renewable capacity and diversify beyond its traditional lignite mining and thermal power businesses

  • NLC India has been transferring renewable assets to the unit ahead of its planned listing as it pursues a capacity expansion target of 18 gigawatts of renewable energy by 2032

  • The stake sale is part of New Delhi's broader divestment strategy to generate revenue, widen shareholding in public-sector firms and improve governance practices

  • SBI Capital Markets, HDFC Bank, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities and IIFL Capital Services are managing the IPO

($1 = 93.4475 Indian rupees)

data.title: Treasury Yields Fall in Asian Trade, Shrug off Fed Rate Hike Prospect
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields fall in Asian trade on Thursday, even as the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a fast pace.

Minutes of the latest Fed rate-setting meeting, where the Fed left interest rates unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase of half a percentage point in December. The committee's discussion of inflation revealed increasing concern of broadening price pressure amid strong growth in economic activity, Stuart Paul, U.S. economist at UBS, said in a note.

The minutes pushed higher market expectations of a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike on the Dec. 9 meeting. Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and an 8% likelihood of a 50-basis-point tightening, according to LSEG. A 50-basis-point high was priced with a 2% probability on Wednesday.

"Strong data since the meeting is likely to have strengthened the case for further tightening and we see it as likely that members will indicate another rate increase in their projections in December," Elisabet Kopelman, U.S. economist and Fed watcher at SEB said. "We stick to our view of one more rate increase in December but risks are clearly skewed for another increase, possibly in March," she said.

The two-year Treasury yield slipped 0.4 basis points to 4.795%, while the 10-year Treasury yield declined also 0.4 basis point to 5.061%, according to Tradeweb.

The Treasury will conduct a $19 billion auction of 10-year Treasury inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, on Thursday.

Despite the backdrop of higher real yields, cheap valuations, and improving liquidity, J.P. Morgan analysts think the hawkish Fed backdrop and amount of supply in the 10-year sector means the auction "will need more of a concession to be digested smoothly."

Write to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com

data.title: Gold edges up from 14-month low as markets assess Fed rate outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Traders price in 90% chance of a 25-bp Fed hike in December
  • Global platinum market to swing back to deficit next year
  • Break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment- OCBC analysts

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices ticked up on Thursday, after hitting a more-than-one-year low earlier in the session amid growing US interest rate hike bets, while investors looked to Federal Reserve commentary for fresh signals on monetary policy.

Spot gold rose 0.3% to $3,733.76 per ounce by 0630 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,693.13 per ounce earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.1% to $3,737.20.

"It's (gold) making a mild attempt to lift itself, but this is more likely to be profit-taking from bears over any fundamental catalyst," said Matt Simpson, a senior market analyst at StoneX.

Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he's likely to support tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures.

Additionally, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the US central bank needs to respond more aggressively to inflation.

Markets see a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-bp move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

"The break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment. Buying interest remains subdued, while the continued decline raises the risk of further liquidation," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

Meanwhile, the global platinum market will swing back to deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday.

Spot silver rose 0.8% to $45.38 per ounce, platinum gained 0.2% to $1,374.16, and palladium climbed 1.4% to $961.10.

data.title: Novartis narrows mid-term annual sales growth target to 5% through 2031
data.description:
Swiss drugmaker Novartis on Thursday outlined new mid-term sales targets that were at the lower end of the range it had given a year earlier, ahead of its annual investor event in London.

Novartis now expects net sales to grow 5% annually at constant currencies from 2026 through 2031. Previously, the company expected sales growth of 5%-6% through 2030.

Following a string of late-stage study setbacks in September, that drew close scrutiny on CEO Vas Narasimhan's dealmaking strategy, Novartis is now looking to boost investor confidence in its post-2030 growth plans.

Novartis faces a steep patent cliff with blockbusters like heart drug Entresto seeing tough competition from cheaper rivals, raising the question of how it will sustain growth over the next decade, when another top seller, Cosentyx, will lose exclusivity.

The company expects sales from its anti-inflammatory drug Rhapsido, breast cancer drug Kisqali and multiple sclerosis drug Kesimpta, among others, can offset the drop in sales.

Of these, Rhapsido and Kisqali are expected to bring in peak annual sales of $8 billion and $10 billion each.

New experimental medicines, including ianalumab, abelacimab and del-brax, could add further sales.

data.title: ANT Stock’s $1.5T Debut Won’t Immediately Move The Needle For Nasdaq, S&P 500, Says Morningstar — Here’s Why
data.description:
Key points:
  • The market analyst stated that once various lockup periods expire, its weight in the indexes should climb. 
  • Nasdaq and FTSE Russell will wait until their December rebalancing period to include ANT stock, to avoid unnecessary trading.
  • S&P requires new additions to the index to have positive earnings in the most recent quarter and the most recent four quarters combined, meaning that Anthropic’s inclusion will take at least a year.

Anthropic’s public listing, valued at $1.5 trillion at a price of $83 a share, which is above the expected range, is likely to impact index fund holdings following its debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday.

However, Morningstar sees the initial impact on most indexes to be modest, as only a portion of Anthropic’s shares will be publicly tradable.

ANT IPO: Impact On Major Indexes

Morningstar said that most index providers impose float-adjusted market capitalization limits to avoid assigning large weightings to stocks that aren’t easily tradable.

The market analyst noted that the Claude-maker’s shares being sold represent just about 6% of the company, limiting its impact on most indexes.

“Once various lockup periods expire, however, its weight in the indexes should climb,” it said.

Impact On Nasdaq, S&P 500, FTSE Russell 

Morningstar said in its report that the Nasdaq-100 Index’s 2026 methodology update requires a newly public company to rank among the index's top 40 holdings by total market cap for inclusion. While Anthropic qualifies, the AI company will still need to wait at least 15 trading days before being added to the flagship index. This will permit early volatility to shake out before inclusion, it said. However, it also highlighted that Nasdaq has decided to wait until its mid-December rebalancing period to include the stock, to avoid unnecessary trading.

Nasdaq is among the few index providers that use total market cap instead of float-adjusted market cap to weight holdings, and Morningstar said that its multiplier will give Anthropic more weight than most.

Meanwhile, S&P requires new additions to the index to have positive earnings in the most recent quarter and the most recent four quarters combined, meaning that Anthropic’s inclusion will take at least a year.

However, its broader benchmarks, including the S&P Total Market Index, the Dow Jones US Total Stock Market Index, and their subindexes, can include a stock with either a minimum float of 10% or a float-adjusted market cap equal to at least 10% of the total market cap of the 100th-largest company in the index.

Anthropic’s float is about 6%, but it would likely clear the second test, Morningstar said, adding that its float would likely increase as lockup periods expire.

“If Anthropic meets the stricter criteria of the S&P 500, index funds tracking the benchmark will likely need to buy billions of dollars of the stock. Active managers measured against the index may have to add it, too, to limit tracking error relative to the benchmark,” it said.

FTSE Russell’s new fast-entry rule allows large IPOs into its indexes after five trading days, but it applies to larger IPOs with float-adjusted market caps that rank in the top 500.

FTSE Russell is also expected to wait until the December semiannual reconstitution to avoid liquidity problems near the Thanksgiving holiday.

Retail Stance On Anthropic And Market Indexes

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ANT stock was already ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing amid ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

Meanwhile, retail sentiment around SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) and iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) was ‘bullish.’

data.title: Rupee nudges higher as sustained inflows shield against firmer dollar
data.description:
By Jaspreet Kalra

The Indian rupee was modestly stronger on Thursday as sustained foreign flows into Indian equities helped the currency counter pressure from a stronger dollar, buoyed by growing expectations of a hawkish US interest rate outlook.

The rupee rose 0.1% from its previous close to 93.34 per dollar, lingering around its closest level in seven months.

The momentum in equity inflows reflected in early morning dollar sales by foreign lenders, traders said. Overseas investors have net bought $11.3 billion of Indian stocks so far in November, on track for a record month of inflows.

The surge in dollar supply, which occurs when overseas investors buy rupees against the dollar to buy local stocks, has helped the rupee hold its strengthen despite a near 2% rise in the dollar index this month.

Traders have also pointed to an unwinding of bearish rupee wagers that have kept the currency at a modest premium in the non-deliverable forward market compared with prevailing levels for onshore forwards.

Still, markets are watching for a pickup in dollar conversions by exporters, which have remained subdued for much of 2026, as they are expected to further bolster the currency.

"USD/INR has broken below the 94-97 range that held for much of the past 6-7 months. Exporters now have less incentive to hold USD receipts in anticipation of a weaker INR. A further fall in USD/INR would increase conversion and bring April’s low of 92.4 into view," DBS said in a note.

Elsewhere, Asian currencies were trading mixed while regional stocks slumped as fears over the AI trade and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials left sentiment fragile ahead of an eagerly awaited market debut from Anthropic.

Money markets have fully priced in a Fed rate hike next month, with 90% odds of a 25-bp hike and a 10% chance of a 50-bp increase, per the CME's FedWatch tool.
